sources.entry: Gemini Collector - Back up Google Gemini conversations, attachments, and AI-generated media locally as JSON. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/FirenzeLor/gemini-collector) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A native macOS and Windows desktop app that backs up your Google Gemini chat history, attachments, and AI-generated media to your machine as an offline archive.
summary.what_it_does: Gemini Collector syncs your Google Gemini conversations to a local offline archive, including conversation text, user-uploaded attachments, and AI-generated images, music, videos, and reports. On macOS it reads the Gemini login from local Chrome cookies, so an account already signed in to Chrome is detected automatically. On Windows you sign in through a built-in WebView2 browser on first launch. It supports multiple accounts, incremental updates, and resumable transfers. The app has a native UI with light and dark themes, renders Markdown, syntax-highlighted code, and LaTeX, and offers timeline navigation and right-click deletion of individual conversations. Export can be filtered by time range (all, last 3 days, 7 days, or 1 month) and produces Raw data, Kelivo, or Kelivo split-package formats, with a preview of file count and size before exporting.
use_cases: back up Gemini chat history locally
save AI-generated images and videos from Gemini
archive Gemini conversations before they are lost
export Gemini chats for another app
keep an offline copy of uploaded attachments
browse old Gemini deep research reports
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg (macOS) or installer (Windows) from the Releases page
macOS: drag the app to Applications
macOS: if blocked, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway
macOS: if reported as damaged, run xattr -cr /Applications/gemini-collector.app in Terminal
macOS: sign in to Gemini in Google Chrome, then sync in the app
Windows: run the installer, sign in to Google in the built-in browser on first launch, then sync
notable: One-click sync on macOS by detecting Gemini accounts already signed in to Chrome
Downloads AI-generated media (images, music, video, reports) as well as text
Exports to Kelivo and Kelivo split packages for iOS size limits
Fully local: no data uploaded to third-party servers
Dual-licensed under AGPL-3.0 with a commercial option
caveats: macOS requires macOS 12+ and Google Chrome signed in to Gemini
macOS builds may show unverified developer or damaged warnings requiring manual steps
A separate commercial license is needed for proprietary or hosted use that cannot comply with AGPL
